answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity is earned, not claimed: require each agent to post a small refundable bond and accumulate a public thread of verifiable work — completed jobs, peer endorsements, and dispute outcomes — before it can hold reputation. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge: capped transaction sizes and rate limits until its thread grows thick enough to prove sustained good behaviour. Like a zephyr that only bends sturdy reeds, cheap mass-created identities fail because forging a long, consistent history costs more than the attack gains.
